5-SULFOSALICYLIC ACID-ANCHORED SNO2 NANOPARTICLES FOR WATER PURIFICATION: SYNTHESIS, MICROSTRUCTURE, AND RAMAN SPECTRAL ANALYSIS

ABSTRACT

The concept of modifying nanomaterials to enhance their properties through chemical treatment is a key area of research in nanotechnology today. This article aimed to investigate the role of 5-sulfosalicylic acid (5-SSA) in modifying the crystal structure, enhancing surface properties, and potentially influencing the vibrational behavior of tin dioxide (SnO2) nanoparticles prepared using the sol-gel method. The effect of acid treatment was investigated by characterizing the nanomaterial using several tests, including X-ray diffraction (XRD), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), Raman spectroscopy, and surface area analysis. The results showed that the rutile phase of the tin(II) oxide (SnO2) nanoparticles in the virgin sample remained unchanged in the treated sample according to XRD analysis, while the surface area of the virgin nanoparticles decreased by 20% due to the acid treatment. FTIR analysis indicated that acid treatment stabilized the functional groups of the organic compounds, while vibrational patterns were enhanced across additional ranges due to surface defects and impurities, as well as photonic effects, as confirmed by Raman spectra. Furthermore, contact of the nanomaterial with the organic acid resulted in similar effects on the photo-response, significantly increasing the potential for photocurrent generation. The study’s findings confirm that the treatment of tin (II) oxide (SnO2) nanoparticles with 5-sulfosalicylic acid (5-SSA) not only modifies the surface but also enhances the crystalline and vibrational properties of the treated material.
